correctness.rationale: Lewko's finite Fourier block is discretized on a sufficiently fine prime cyclic group, where every progression step from the original finite frequency range is invertible. The two-copy cyclic system is completed by a signed companion block, giving exactly 2M mutually orthonormal unimodular vectors on 2M atoms. For an arbitrary ordering of all basis vectors, restricting to the distinguished first-copy columns recovers Lewko's two-ordering combinatorial lemma; all other coefficients are set to zero, so the positive-proportion maximal-partial-sum obstruction survives.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Lewko proves the finite counterexample on a nonatomic two-copy torus and separately completes the infinite construction, but does not state a finite atomic complete-basis or Butson-Hadamard version. Searches for finite-group, finite-atomic, complex-Hadamard, Butson, and Fourier-matrix formulations of the Garsia counterexample found no matching theorem. Residual risk remains because the strengthening is short once the recent two-copy construction is known.

value.rationale: The result shows that neither incompleteness nor nonatomicity is responsible for the failure of Garsia's universal rearrangement bound: the obstruction persists in square complete unimodular bases encoded by a rigid Butson-Hadamard matrix. It also yields infinitely many finite matrix orders for every fixed threshold.
